lines: I grew up in Quito, Ecuador, a city in the Andes. I left to study in the United States and stayed to follow the American dream.
I studied computer science and business, then earned an MBA.
Today I am an agent architect. I design AI agents from the first sketch to the last test. An agent will answer with the same confidence whether it knows or not, so I measure what mine do.
This site is that habit turned on my own ideas. One agent builds and a different one checks. The agents write most of the code.
I lift, I play golf, and I read philosophy and theology.
I did not get here alone. I am grateful to God and to the people who helped me.

help.intro: For most closed ideas, more data would not change the answer: the price already had it, as far as the test could tell, or the market was too small. For a few, it might:

items.text: A dated daily history of song streaming counts, or the storage and machine time to record one forward. One music-chart idea passed its volume check and stopped there, for lack of that history.
The settled winners for the 43.7% of heavy-favorite outcomes on Novig that could not be scored.
A futures order book you could have traded at, with coin borrow costs, to measure the bitcoin futures basis.
A licensed round-the-clock price feed for off-hours commodity markets. Even with it, a fair answer may take years.
A second checker: someone who tests the same kind of thing and would check a case.

intro: My trading research is where I learned the method: write the test down first, then close each idea with its proof.
vet-bench turns that method into a test for AI agents.
Its traps are built on the ways those results went wrong.
